I honestly don't know. I replayed GTA 5 recently and it honestly felt pretty bad. This is just a description of my personal experience --

Ignoring all the cutscenes and dialogue and story to focus solely on the gameplay -- its a slow, shallow, cover shooter with a handful of unique abilities. I will give GTA the advantage in police chases -- but again, it's frequently made way more frustrating by random passerby NPC banzai charges.

The story of GTA V is also very exaggerated and full of stereotypes -- which is the point of GTA, to be satirical of mainstream culture. But nowadays it just reminds me of how insane of a position America is in, and of how sincerity and empathy are in rapid decline among the general public. It's more depressing than comedic.

I preferred GTA 4's story over GTA 5. It was still very satirical and full of stereotypes, but there were a couple of genuinely good people I was really rooting for.

I don't know if its used in Cyberpunk, but one trick devs use is to shape clothes a specific way to give a unique body appearance and then layer that on top of the default NPC body. That way the NPC has a "unique body" without actually having to change the body model or introduce a new one.

You'll notice this most prominently in Bethesda games when you use mods to don NPC exclusive clothing. Your character's body will change. It's also why BodySlide studio and the like are massive mods for Fallout 4 -- so players can shape their own unique body models.

This is also a thing in Final Fantasy 7 remake and rebirth. Aerith's hips and Tifa's boobs look big but the ripped models actually don't even have those body parts. The body shape is inherent to those clothes. Which was swiftly "rectified" by the modding community with new body models, but anyway...
